answer.generated: In the dining philosophers problem, five philosophers sit around a table each holding a fork, creating a situation where mutual exclusion prevents simultaneous use of two forks by one philosopher. Hold and wait occurs when each philosopher picks up one fork and waits for the other, causing circular wait among all five. No preemption cannot resolve this cycle, so deadlock ensues. To prevent deadlock, a solution could be to assign a global ordering (e.g., odd/even philosopher numbers) so that only one philosopher picks up a fork at a time, breaking the circular wait condition. Alternatively, resource allocation could be restricted to allow at most four philosophers to pick up a fork, preventing the hold and wait pattern.
